raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Repeated `/v1/decisions` requests retain per-request state in the native MLX runner. These requests use `max_new_tokens=0` and finish during prefill. The scheduler releases their KV resources, but does not notify the worker. The existing decode-only cleanup never runs if subsequent batches are also prefill-only.

A similar cleanup was proposed in [#32446](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32446). It was briefly cherry-picked onto the [#30578 branch](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30578#issuecomment-5099972233), then reverted as scope creep and hard to review ([revert note](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30578#issuecomment-5233089096)); it was not merged.

## Modifications

Call the existing optional worker release hook when a request finishes during prefill. The MLX worker records the finished request IDs and removes their state before the next fresh non-idle launch, including EXTEND.

Removal is deferred because an already-launched overlap decode may still need the state during finalization. The fresh-launch boundary lets that work finish before cleanup and removes old state before routing new requests, including requests that reuse the same ID.

This does not address idle-tail retention or abort/retraction cleanup. The tracking stays in the native MLX worker and can be removed with that backend as part of #32321 / #36164.

## Accuracy Tests

The targeted routing and result-processor suites pass: 36 tests and 4 subtests.

Coverage includes zero-token completion, immediate request-ID reuse, pending chained-decode finalization before cleanup, live and chunked requests, and workers without the optional hook.

The overlap test runs the real event loop with mocked model execution and KV allocation/release. It checks lifecycle ordering, not physical pool-reuse or Metal correctness. No model-quality benchmark was run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

A sequential HTTP memory check compared base `57c81258d` with fix `021ea7ae0`. Later commits only changed tests and comments.

| Measured outcome | Base `57c81258d` | Fix `021ea7ae0` |
|---|---:|---:|
| Successful measured HTTP 200 responses | 20 | 40 |
| Retained request caches, matched requests 1–20 | 6 → 25 | 1 throughout |
| MLX active memory, matched requests 1–20 | 2.920 → 11.233 GiB | 0.733–0.801 GiB |

![Request-cache and memory trends for repeated prefill-only /v1/decisions requests](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a57ac194-f04d-46ad-81ef-cb7d0e779223)

This run used concurrency one and disabled radix caching. It checks request-state retention, not throughput. Environment details and measurement limits are below.

<details>
<summary>Environment details and measurement limits</summary>

- **Machine:** Mac16,8, 48 GiB unified memory, macOS 26.5.2. Python 3.11.12, Torch 2.13.0, Transformers 5.12.1, MLX 0.32.3.
- **Model:** `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-MLX-4bit`, snapshot `173234aa840d113125e9f2271100ddbaf16c9620` for both runs.
- **Flags:** `SGLANG_USE_MLX=1`, `SGLANG_MLX_CACHE_LIMIT_GB=2`, `--mlx-enable-sampling`, `--context-length 512`, `--max-running-requests 1`, `--disable-radix-cache`; overlap enabled.
- **Workload:** three client warmups per run, followed by sequential one-question binary-choice requests with 216 prompt tokens each. The first 20 measured inputs matched; the fixed run continued through request 40.
- **Measurement:** identical worker hooks recorded `_req_caches` and `mx.get_active_memory()` after prefill; HTTP access logs confirmed responses. System-available memory is plotted where retained. Base request 20 returned HTTP 200 and its worker counters are recorded, but its latency and system-available-memory sample were not retained.
- **Limits:** automatic token pools differed (149,630 base; 168,005 fix). This is not a capacity or speed comparison. The baseline was stopped after request 20; the operator reported the configured safety guard fired, but its console output was not retained. The run was not continued to OOM. The result covers one model, concurrency one, and radix caching disabled.

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). Checked changed files with Ruff/isort and `git diff --check`; the full pre-commit suite was not run.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No public API/configuration change.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Model-quality and throughput benchmarks were not run; the bounded memory check is described above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+        self._process_prefill(worker, [self._req("same")])
+
+        new_req = _FakeReq("same")
+        batch = _FakeBatch(ForwardMode.EXTEND, [new_req], [2])
+        launch = worker.async_forward_batch_generation_mlx(batch)
+
+        self.assertEqual(runner.ops_for("same"), ["remove_request", "prefill_start"])
+        self.assertEqual(worker._mlx_active_rids, {"same"})
+        self.assertFalse(worker._mlx_finished_rids)
+        self.assertEqual(len(launch.prefills), 1)
+        self.assertFalse(launch.extends)
+        self.assertIsNot(launch.prefills[0].cache, old_cache)
+        worker.finalize_mlx_result(launch, [new_req])
+
+    def test_retracted_prefill_completion_releases_runner_state(self):
+        """A prefill-only request completing after retraction must not leave
+        runner state behind when the next prefill wave starts."""
+        worker = self._worker({"retracted"})
+        runner = worker._mlx_runner
+        req = self._req("retracted")
+        req.retraction_count = 1
+        req.full_untruncated_fill_ids = array("q", [1, 2])
+        launch = worker.async_forward_batch_generation_mlx(
+            _FakeBatch(ForwardMode.EXTEND, [req], [2])
+        )
+        worker.finalize_mlx_result(launch, [req])
+        runner._known.add(req.rid)  # the new prefill finalized
+        runner._req_caches[req.rid] = launch.prefills[0].cache
+        self._process_prefill(worker, [req])
+
+        worker.async_forward_batch_generation_mlx(
+            _FakeBatch(ForwardMode.EXTEND, [_FakeReq("fresh")], [2])
+        )
+
+        self.assertTrue(req.finished())
+        self.assertFalse(runner.has_request(req.rid))
+        self.assertNotIn(req.rid, runner._req_caches)
+        self.assertNotIn(req.rid, worker._req_retraction_count)
+        self.assertEqual(worker._mlx_active_rids, {"fresh"})
+        self.assertFalse(worker._mlx_finished_rids)
+
+    def test_overlap_drains_chained_decode_before_mixed_launch_cleanup(self):
+        import mlx.core as mx
+
+        from sglang.srt.hardware_backend.mlx.model_runner import MlxModelRunner
+        from sglang.srt.hardware_backend.mlx.scheduler_mixin import (
+            SchedulerMlxOverlapMixin,
+        )
+
+        events = []
+        worker = self._worker({"finished", "live"})
+        runner = worker._mlx_runner
+        # Sync while the request owns its row; removing state after a chained
+        # decode drains must not write through a row the scheduler has reused.
+        runner.disable_radix_cache = False
+        runner._cache_layout = SimpleNamespace(
+            has_auxiliary_state=False,
+            first_attention_layer_index=0,
+            full_attention_layer_indices=[0],
+        )
+        runner._cache_pool = []
+        runner._req_token_ids = {rid: [1, 2] for rid in runner._known}
+        runner._req_sampling = {}
+        runner._req_pool_idx = {"finished": 0, "live": 1}
+        runner._req_synced_offset = {rid: 1 for rid in runner._known}
+        runner._req_to_token_pool = SimpleNamespace(
+            req_to_token=torch.arange(8).reshape(2, 4)
+        )
+        runner._attention_kv_pool = Mock()
+        for rid in runner._known:
+            state = mx.zeros((1, 1, 2, 1))
+            runner._req_caches[rid] = [
+                SimpleNamespace(keys=state, values=state, offset=2, state=[state])
+            ]
+        for name in (
+            "_sync_decode_kv_to_pool",
+            "_sync_new_kv_to_pool",
+            "_first_attention_cache",
+            "_release_cache",
+            "release_request_row",
+        ):
+            setattr(runner, name, getattr(MlxModelRunner, name).__get__(runner))
+
+        def remove(rid):
+            events.append(("remove", rid))
+            MlxModelRunner.remove_request(runner, rid)
+            runner._known.discard(rid)
+
+        runner.remove_request = remove
+        original_decode_start = runner.decode_batch_start
+        original_prefill_start = runner.prefill_start
+
+        def chain(previous):
+            events.append(("chain", None))
+            pending = original_decode_start(previous.req_ids)
+            pending.lazy_tokens = previous.lazy_tokens + 1
+            pending.chained = True
+            return pending
+
+        def finalize(pending):
+            pending.lazy_tokens.tolist()
+            if getattr(pending, "chained", False):
+                # Both requests' state must survive the first result's finish
+                # notification until the already-launched decode has drained.
+                self.assertTrue(runner.has_request("finished"))
+                self.assertTrue(runner.has_request("live"))
+                events.append(("finalize_chain", None))
+            return [3] * len(pending.req_ids)
+
+        def prefill(**kwargs):
+            events.append(("prefill", kwargs["req_id"]))
+            return original_prefill_start(**kwargs)
+
+        runner.decode_batch_start_chained = chain
+        runner.decode_batch_finalize = finalize
+        runner.prefill_start = prefill
+
+        # Fake computation still needs to publish the new request's state at
+        # the same boundary as MlxModelRunner.prefill_finalize.
+        def prefill_finalize(pending):
+            runner._known.add(pending.req_id)
+            runner._req_caches[pending.req_id] = pending.cache
+            pending.cache[0].offset = 2
+            runner._req_synced_offset[pending.req_id] = 2
+            runner._req_pool_idx[pending.req_id] = 0
+            return 3
+
+        runner.prefill_finalize = prefill_finalize
+        finished = self._req("finished", max_new_tokens=1)
+        live = self._req("live", max_new_tokens=8)
+        fresh = self._req("fresh")
+        for req in (finished, live, fresh):
+            req.return_logprob = False
+            req.full_untruncated_fill_ids = array("q", [1, 2])
+            req.extend_end = 2
+            req.prefix_len = 0
+            req.kv.kv_committed_len = 2
+
+        def batch(mode, reqs, lengths, decoding_reqs=None):
+            out = ScheduleBatch(reqs=reqs)
+            out.forward_mode = mode
+            out.extend_lens = lengths
+            out.decoding_reqs = decoding_reqs
+            out.input_ids = torch.arange(sum(lengths))
+            out.out_cache_loc = torch.arange(sum(lengths))
+            out.return_logprob = False
+            out.enable_overlap = True
+            out.spec_algorithm = SimpleNamespace(is_none=lambda: True)
+            return out
+
+        decode = batch(ForwardMode.DECODE, [finished, live], [1, 1])
+        mixed = batch(ForwardMode.MIXED, [fresh, live], [2, 1], [live])
+        processor = self._processor(worker, overlap=True, tree_cache=Mock())
+        scheduler = SchedulerMlxOverlapMixin()
+        scheduler.tp_worker = worker
+        scheduler.forward_ct = 0
+        scheduler._sched_idled = False
+        scheduler.gracefully_exit = False
+        scheduler._engine_paused = False
+        scheduler.waiting_queue = []
+        scheduler.result_queue = deque()
+        scheduler.running_batch = decode
+        scheduler.last_batch = None
+        scheduler.profiler_manager = Mock()
+        scheduler.future_map = Mock()
+        scheduler.ingest_requests = Mock()
+        scheduler.invariant_checker = Mock()
+        scheduler.get_next_batch_to_run = Mock(
+            side_effect=[
+                SimpleNamespace(running_batch=decode, batch_to_run=decode),
+                SimpleNamespace(running_batch=mixed, batch_to_run=mixed),
+                StopIteration,
+            ]
+        )
+
+        def process(batch, result):
+            if batch.forward_mode.is_decode():
+                processor.process_batch_result_decode(batch, result)
+            else:
+                processor.process_batch_result_prefill(batch, result)
+
+        scheduler.process_batch_result = process
+
+        def release(req, *_args, **_kwargs):
+            self.assertIn(req.rid, worker._mlx_finished_rids)
+            self.assertTrue(runner.has_request(req.rid))
+            self.assertNotIn(req.rid, runner._req_pool_idx)
+            if req.rid == "finished":
+                writes = runner._attention_kv_pool.set_kv_all_layers.call_args_list
+                self.assertEqual([call.args[0].tolist() for call in writes], [[1]])
+                runner._req_to_token_pool.req_to_token[0] = torch.tensor([8, 9, 10, 11])
+            events.append(("finish", req.rid))
+
+        module = "sglang.srt.managers.scheduler_components.batch_result_processor"
+        with (
+            get_context().override_server_args(
+                disable_radix_cache=False, disable_overlap_schedule=False
+            ),
+            patch(f"{module}.release_kv_cache", side_effect=release),
+            patch(f"{module}.checkpoint_kv_cache"),
+            patch(
+                "sglang.srt.hardware_backend.mlx.scheduler_mixin.resolve_forward_inputs"
+            ),
+            self.assertRaises(StopIteration),
+        ):
+            scheduler.event_loop_overlap_mlx()
+
+        self.assertLess(
+            events.index(("chain", None)), events.index(("finish", "finished"))
+        )
+        self.assertLess(
+            events.index(("finish", "finished")), events.index(("finalize_chain", None))
+        )
+        self.assertLess(
+            events.index(("finalize_chain", None)), events.index(("remove", "finished"))
+        )
+        self.assertLess(
+            events.index(("remove", "finished")), events.index(("prefill", "fresh"))
+        )
+        self.assertNotIn(("remove", "live"), events)
+        self.assertEqual(worker._mlx_active_rids, {"live", "fresh"})
+        self.assertEqual(worker._mlx_finished_rids, {"fresh"})
+        self.assertFalse(live.finished())
+        pool_writes = runner._attention_kv_pool.set_kv_all_layers.call_args_list
+        self.assertEqual([call.args[0].tolist() for call in pool_writes], [[1]])
+        self.assertNotIn("finished", worker._req_retraction_count)
+        self.assertEqual(len(scheduler.result_queue), 0)
+
+    def test_generation_finished_during_prefill_is_marked(self):
+        worker = self._worker({"a"})
+        self._process_prefill(worker, [self._req("a", max_new_tokens=1)])
+        self.assertEqual(worker._mlx_finished_rids, {"a"})
+
+    def test_unfinished_and_middle_prefills_are_not_marked(self):
+        worker = self._worker({"unfinished", "middle"})
+        unfinished = self._req("unfinished", max_new_tokens=2)
+        middle = self._req("middle")
+        middle.inflight_middle_chunks = 1
+
+        released = self._process_prefill(worker, [unfinished, middle])
+
+        released.assert_not_called()
+        self.assertEqual(worker._mlx_finished_rids, set())
+        self.assertEqual(worker._mlx_runner._known, {"unfinished", "middle"})
+        self.assertFalse(unfinished.finished())
+        self.assertFalse(middle.finished())
+
+    def test_prefill_completion_without_worker_hook(self):
+        req = self._req("a")
+        released = self._process_prefill(SimpleNamespace(), [req])
+        self.assertTrue(req.finished())
+        released.assert_called_once_with(req, None, checkpoint=True)
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
